summary.short: Proposed French statute adding Art. L. 331-4-1 to the Intellectual Property Code. In civil disputes, a protected work is presumed used by an AI model or system provider, unless proven otherwise, once an indicium makes that use plausible. Applies to pending proceedings at entry into force, subject to final judgments.
summary.long: Single-article bill (first reading, committee text, registered 2 June 2026). Paragraph I 1° inserts Art. L. 331-4-1 into the Intellectual Property Code: in any civil dispute, a work or protected subject matter under copyright or related rights is presumed, unless proven otherwise, to have been used by the provider of an AI model or system, once an indicium relating to the development or deployment of the system or to its generated output makes that use plausible. Paragraph I 2° replaces a reference to Law No. 2021-1382 in Art. L. 811-1-1 (1°) with a reference to the new law. Paragraph II makes the presumption in 1° applicable to proceedings pending at the date of entry into force, subject to decisions that have become final. The text sets no administrative authority, sanction or penalty.

relations.note: Art. I 1° inserts a new article L. 331-4-1 into section 1 of chapter Ier, title III, book III, part one. Art. I 2° also amends the reference in L. 811-1-1 1°. Target is not in the registry, so the ID is empty.

notes: Text of the Commission des affaires culturelles et de l’éducation, annex to the report, first reading, article unique (non modifié). The replacement wording in I 2° reads “n° du” with the number and date left blank. Section II applies I 1° to proceedings pending on the entry into force date, except decisions that have become final. The Code de la propriété intellectuelle is not a registry instrument.

thresholds.note: The bill contains no numeric cutoff. Its operative provision (Art. L. 331-4-1 CPI, as inserted by Article unique I.1°) turns on a qualitative evidentiary test, an indication making use 'vraisemblable' (plausible), and the transitional clause (Article unique II) applies by reference to pending proceedings, not to a number.
